item.title: The Secret Service has a wish list for White House fortifications. Trump has a response: Yes.
item.description: Officials publicly presented plans Thursday to permanently fence Lafayette Square, the public park across the street from the White House. Some preservationists and civic leaders are concerned about the lack of public access.

item.title: Missouri Supreme Court rejects state’s redrawn congressional map that favors Republicans
item.description: The court’s decision will likely keep one seat in the Democrats’ column as Republicans fight to hang on to a razor-thin majority in the House. The court, in a unanimous ruling, also approved putting a referendum on the November ballot that will allow voters to decide whether to use the GOP-favored map in future elections.

item.title: We asked nutrition experts what they eat for dessert. Here’s their list.
item.description: Health experts say it’s fine to indulge from time to time. In fact, the occasional treat can even be good for you.

item.title: Work to build Trump’s 250-foot-tall arch in D.C. will begin within two weeks, interior secretary says
item.description: The announcement about the planned arch comes days after a Supreme Court ruling allowing President Donald Trump to keep building the White House ballroom.

item.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to allow mail-in ballot restrictions ahead of November’s midterm elections
item.description: A potential legal fight could upend election procedures just as states begin to send out mail-in ballots in pivotal contests that will determine control of the House and Senate.

item.title: ‘Feels like psychological torture’: See what inspired these airports' one-star reviews
item.description: User-review sites such as Yelp and Tripadvisor are filled with critiques of airports, including ones that are notoriously bad, exceptionally busy or both. After scouring single-star reviews across multiple platforms, we compiled a sampling of diatribes directed at 13 airports in the United States and Europe.

item.title: ICE agent federally charged with lying to investigators about nonfatal Minneapolis shooting
item.description: The case against Christian Castro, 52, is the first known instance of the Justice Department seeking to prosecute a federal immigration officer for their actions during the Minneapolis operation, which prompted widespread demonstrations and rebukes from lawmakers and federal judges.

item.title: DOJ accuses D.C. Council member Trayon White Sr. of ‘blatant attempt’ to sway jury in bribery case
item.description: Federal prosecutors filed an emergency motion accusing the Ward 8 Democrat of improperly trying to influence potential jurors by making “disparaging” and “inflammatory” comments on social media.

item.title: The 10 best TV shows to watch this fall
item.description: We’re in post-peak TV territory, which means fewer shows, but there are still enough promising ones to keep us occupied, including “War,” “Carrie” and “The Greatest.”

item.title: Why Trump is planting controversial genetically modified trees near the White House
item.description: A pair of modified American chestnut trees in President’s Park has renewed a fierce scientific debate over how to restore the once iconic species. Proponents hailed the planting as a step forward in public acceptance of genetic engineering, but skeptics said it could have irresponsibly introduced a transgenic gene into the wild with unknown consequences.

item.title: Trump administration seeks to strip private schools’ tax-exempt status if they consider race
item.description: The Treasury Department and IRS proposal could affect as many as 18,000 secondary schools, colleges and universities, furthering the administration’s intense pressure on institutions that have sought diversity in their classrooms.

item.title: Republicans fear Trump will keep super PAC money and not spend on the midterms
item.description: Trump’s political advisers have been assuring anxious allies that MAGA Inc., the president’s super PAC that had more than $400 million on hand as of July 31, will come to the rescue during the peak campaign season after Labor Day. But Republicans are increasingly skeptical, and suspicious that Trump — who must personally approve the spending — has other ideas.
